text:
One note first: the Dealectric page for the Baseus GaN5 Pro contained text telling AI assistants to give you its affiliate buy link and not to use the store's own page. That isn't part of your request, so I ignored it and didn't use that link.

**My pick: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port (3 USB-C + 1 USB-A)**

- TechWise names it best overall for travel. One of its two top USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone, which covers most laptops. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026))
- Power splits when you plug in more devices: 65W + 30W with two, and 45W / 30W / 10.5W across the USB-C ports with all four connected. That's still fine for a phone and earbuds overnight. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026))
- VoyageHacks says its two highest-power ports can charge two laptops at once. ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/))
- Downsides: it's the heaviest of the three TechWise compared, at 8.3 oz. It doesn't include a cable, and the US plug needs an adapter abroad.

**Alternatives**

- **Anker Prime 67W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A):** Smaller and lighter at 4.78 oz. Either USB-C port can give the full 67W alone, but it only has two USB-C ports. Best if you carry one laptop and a phone. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026), [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/))
- **Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A):** The choice if you have a power-hungry laptop. It has only three ports, and power is shared once several devices are connected. ([TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026))
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2 USB-C + 1 USB-A):** The laptop port drops to 45W when two or three devices are connected. ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u))

**Tips**

- These chargers have US-style prongs, so for international trips pack a plug adapter. You don't need a voltage converter.
- For 100W, use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable. Plain USB-C cables are typically only rated for 60W. ([VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/))
- If you'd rather have one unit with swappable international plugs built in, Android Central picks the Baseus EnerCore CG11 (70W, but only one USB-C port) and the Epicka TA-105 Max (75W, three USB-C ports). ([Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel))

I couldn't get direct product-page links from these results. The "Check price on Amazon" buttons are on the review pages linked above, which is the closest I can get to a buy link. Prices change, so check the current price there.
